newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CONTROVERSIAL REFEREE TO TAKE CHARGE OF REAL-BARCELONA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CONTROVERSIAL REFEREE TO TAKE CHARGE OF REAL-BARCELONA.

text.p: Juan Manuel Brito Arceo, Spain's most controversial referee, will take charge of next month's eagerly-awaited Real Madrid-Barcelona clash.
Arceo gained notoriety in December 1989 after television replays showed he had awarded a penalty against Barcelona for a foul committed two metres outside the area.

Barcelona lost 4-3 to Sevilla and in the next game at the Camp Nou enraged fans let loose a pig wearing a collar with Arceo's name on it. He was also bombarded with obscene calls after a banner with his home number was unfurled in the stadium.

Arceo has been at the centre of several other controversies since, most notably in 1991 when he sent off four Atletico Madrid players in one game. Outspoken Atletico president Jesus Gil was fined three million pesetas (now $23,800) because of insulting comments made in the wake of the incident.

Atletico's game at Espanyol last season ended with Arceo being carried off after being hit in the groin by an orange. Despite claims of over-reaction, football authorities punished Espanyol by closing the Sarria stadium for one game.
Arceo said he was delighted to be picked for the biggest fixture in the Spanish game and that he would "kiss the computer" that had chosen him.
But within hours of saying he would keep a low profile Arceo found himself at the centre of another row after failing to award Sevilla a penalty in Wednesday's Cup game with Malaga.
"I know the Santiago Bernabeu stadium will be full but it's not something that worries me," said Arceo.
Fans who have applied for tickets to see the game on December 7could fill the 106,00-capacity ground three times over.
The 450-seat press box has been similarly over-subscribed by a deluge of international reporters.
"We've never seen this before," said Real administrator Manuel Fernandez Trigo, "Real has 1,000 supporters' clubs and we've had ticket requests from 688."
Season ticket holders will have to pay an additional 3,000 pesetas ($24) to stand, while the most expensive seats will cost 14,000 pesetas ($111). Black market prices are expected to be much higher.
